A browser roguelike in Dart: a town to rest in, a dungeon of a hundred depths, and heroes that keep their gear between dives.

About the game

Hauberk is a roguelike by Bob Nystrom (munificent), written in Dart for the browser and copyright 2000–2014 and still being worked on. You create a hero (race and class), start in a town with a home and shops, and pick a depth to dive to: up to one level deeper than you have been so far, a hundred in all. Every level is a fresh dungeon; leave it by an exit (q) to return to town with what you found. Experience is not automatic levelling: you spend it (Shift+E) on your stats and skills. The game is unfinished, but very playable.

Keyboard controls

The keys to remember

h
The game's own help screen
Shift+H
Auto-explore: walk to unexplored places (any key stops)
Enter
Menu of all commands
b
Inventory with a cursor: Enter = everything you can do with the item
q
Walk to the nearest known exit; press again on it to leave the level
Esc
Cancel, close a dialog

Saving your game

  • Hauberk saves your heroes when you leave a level (back to town or deeper), when you leave a shop or your home, and when you change items in town. The middle of a dive is not saved: closing the page then loses what happened since the last save.
  • In the browser the heroes, window layout and settings live in this browser's storage (IndexedDB). File ▾ → Export save downloads them (hauberk-heroes.json), Import save loads them back. Private windows and "clear site data" delete them: export first.
  • Death with the Stairs setting returns the hero to the last save; with Permanent the hero is deleted.

Tips

  • Bring a light: deep levels are dark, and auto-explore refuses to walk blind. Torches and lanterns are sold in town.
  • Spend experience (Shift+E) after every dive; unspent experience does nothing.
  • Take the exit (q walks you there) before the level gets too hot: forfeiting (Shift+F) loses everything you found on it.
  • Your home in town stores what you can't carry; sell the rest in the shops.
  • Run (Shift+direction) down corridors, but rest (Shift+L) to full health before opening new rooms.
  • Throw (t) spare weapons and flasks at monsters you would rather not meet in melee.

New player's guide

Your first hero

  • On the hero list press n for a new hero: pick a name, race and class. Death: Stairs means dying loses everything since you last took an exit or entrance; Permanent deletes the hero.
  • You start in town. Walk into the shops to buy (a light first!) and into your home to store items. b shows what you carry.

Diving

  • Step on the dungeon entrance (or press q twice: walk there, step in) and choose a depth.
  • Explore with Shift+H: it stops when a monster or item comes into view or a message appears; any key stops it too.
  • Fight by walking into monsters. Abilities (a) and spells (s) depend on your class and on the experience you spent.
  • When you have had enough, press q: the hero walks to the nearest known exit; press q on it to go back to town with your loot.

Growing stronger

  • Killing monsters earns experience. Shift+E spends it on strength, agility, vitality, intellect and skills.
  • Shift+A shows your hero, equipment and the lore you have gathered on monsters and items.
  • Better gear comes from deeper levels; the shops restock each time you return.

Playing in the browser

  • The map is the game's own screen (DawnLike tiles, or the game's glyphs after Tiles in the top bar); hero, log messages, inventory, equipment and what you see are separate windows. A− / A+ on a title bar (shown on hover) change that window's size of text or tiles; Windows ▾ shows, hides and rearranges them (drag a title bar or the gap between windows). Dialogs and menus appear as text boxes over the map.
  • Keys: the numeric keypad, the arrow keys or the laptop keys i o p k ; , . / move you. The game has no mouse support.
  • Audio ▾: sound effects made for this port (synthesized, one per kind of action), off by default; the choice is remembered. Hauberk has no music.
  • Browsers keep a few shortcuts for themselves (Ctrl+W, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+N, and Cmd shortcuts on a Mac), so those never reach the game.
  • If the game ever crashes, a message appears at the top; reload the page to continue from the last save.

About this version

  • Based on Hauberk by Bob Nystrom, upstream commit munificent/hauberk @ 6c5c684c, MIT licence; compiled to JavaScript with Dart.
  • Tiles: DawnLike by DragonDePlatino, palette by DawnBringer, CC BY 4.0 (OpenGameArt). Sound effects synthesized for this port.
  • Our changes (auto-explore, exit walking, command menu, inventory cursor and item menus, tiles, sound, web page) are on GitHub: memmaker/hauberk (all changes).
